docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:13: `sys create` assembles a system host from the workspace's scaffold records, but it only runs once: any integration scaffolded *after* the host exists is invisible to it, and re-running `sys create` would overwrite the whole directory (`--force`). This plan adds `intropy sys update`, which scans the workspace for **orphaned components** — scaffold records with a block kind that the host's own scaffold record does not mention — and re-renders the host's declaration files to include them, without t... [truncated]
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:26: `sys update` closes that gap. It must be **idempotent** (a second run is a no-op) and **non-destructive** (accept existing identical files, never replace or delete without `--force`, never drop a declared component).
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:39: - R1. `sys update` locates exactly one system host in the workspace and errors when there are zero or several.
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:48: - R10. The workspace scan root is unambiguous: `sys update` requires running from the system/workspace root (the host's parent), and errors clearly when invoked from inside the host directory (review finding 5).
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:66: - `internal/system/create.go` — the command's engine. `Create` scans scaffolds (`template.ListScaffolds`), calls `Assemble`, builds the payload (`buildPayload`), renders via `template.Create` with `OnManifest: requireFactsPayload`, then reads the record back to fill `ProjectName`/`SystemClass` and prints the summary to stderr. `sys update` mirrors the shape but splits prepare from run (below).
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:69: - `internal/template/prepare.go` — **`PrepareCreate` / `RunCreate` (the key seam).** `PrepareCreate` fetches the library, resolves values, and returns a `PreparedCreate` (manifest, values, skeleton root, owner/repo/version, cleanup) with *nothing written*. `RunCreate` renders, processes dependencies, and writes the scaffold record. The dashboard already uses this split to control the render itself; `sys update` uses it the same way — `PrepareCreate`, then a new update-mode render, then its own r... [truncated]
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:79: - The non-destructive-update precedent is stated in `AGENTS.md` for manifest creation: "accepts existing identical files but never replaces or deletes a file." `sys update` adopts the same contract, relaxed only by an explicit `--force`.
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:90: - **Prepare/render/record as three explicit steps, not one `template.Create` call.** `template.Create` renders and writes the record in one flow; `sys update` needs per-file outcomes, dry-run, and the record written *last*. `PrepareCreate` gives the fetch-and-resolve half; the update owns the render (update mode, U2) and the record write (R4) itself, skipping `RunCreate` (review finding 2).
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:94: - **The scan root is the workspace root, enforced.** `sys update` derives the scan root from the located host's parent (the system root) rather than trusting `.`, so running it from inside the host directory errors clearly instead of silently missing sibling components (R10, review finding 5).
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:104: - Should `sys update` overwrite a differing file by default? → **No** (user decision). Differing file is an error naming the file; `--force` opts into overwrite.
docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:196: **Goal:** `system.Update(ctx, UpdateOptions)`: locate host and merge (U1), prepare the template at the record's pin (R8), render in update mode (U2), rewrite the record last (R4), print the summary, honor `--dry-run`/`--output json`, and run the post-update topology validation (R6).

docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-sys-update-orphaned-components-plan.md:243: **Goal:** `intropy sys update` on the command tree, flags plumbed, help text conforming to house style.

**What the error means:** the three files on disk (`Ports.cs`, `OrderNotificationHostDevelopment.cs`, `OrderNotificationHostSystem.cs`) match neither what the template would render now nor what it rendered when the host was created — so they've been hand-edited or drifted since. `sys update` refuses to overwrite them without `--force`, by design. Nothing is written on conflict, so the host record is still consistent.

**To fix it right now:**
- If the edits are intentional: keep them by hand, or run from the workspace root with the CLI: `intropy sys update --force`
- From the dashboard: the sync banner now offers that path directly.

**What I changed in the dashboard** (`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`, `web/src/index.css`): the host-sync error banner previously just printed the message and left you stuck — a dead end, since there was no way to retry with force from the UI. Now, on a 409 (which the API already returns for this exact error, see `syncErrorStatus`), the banner shows a force checkbox and a "Retry with overwrite" button, matching the pattern `CreateDrawer`, `TemplatesView`, and `SeedDrawer` already use. The retry stays disabled until the checkbox is ticked, so overwrite is always deliberate.

# Local-dev tasks for the order-flow SystemHost — the Aspire host that holds the
# system's topology as a typed declaration. `task run` starts the whole system
# (Aspire dashboard, Redis-backed pub/sub, one Dapr sidecar per component); the
# other tasks inspect and export the same model without starting anything.

# HOST is the SystemHost project directory, named after the system.
vars:
  HOST: order-flow

tasks:
  # ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  build:
    desc: Build the SystemHost
    dir: "{{.HOST}}"
    cmds:
      - dotnet build

  # ── Run backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  run:
    desc: Run the system under the Aspire dashboard; stop with Ctrl+C
    dir: "{{.HOST}}"
    cmds:
      - dotnet run

  # ── Generation backend ────────────────────────────────────────────
  check:
    desc: Build and validate the topology without starting anything
    dir: "{{.HOST}}"
    cmds:
      - dotnet run -- check

  # Contract task — see docs/contracts/graph-task.md in the CLI repo. The CLI
  # runs this with --silent and decodes stdout as the topology record, so the
  # record must be the only thing on stdout. `dotnet build` has no flag that
  # fully silences its success summary, so its stdout is redirected to stderr;
  # the run uses --no-build --no-launch-profile, and the task stays silent.
  graph:
    desc: Print the SystemTopology JSON
    dir: "{{.HOST}}"
    silent: true
    cmds:
      - dotnet build -v q >&2
      - dotnet run --no-build --no-launch-profile -- graph

  # Optional contract verb — the development topology (mocks, file
  # connectors). The dashboard shows it when present and hides the view when
  # absent. Same stdout contract as graph.
  graph-development:
    desc: Print the development SystemTopology JSON
    dir: "{{.HOST}}"
    silent: true
    cmds:
      - dotnet build -v q >&2
      - dotnet run --no-build --no-launch-profile -- graph --development

  generate:
    desc: Write Dapr YAML + per-component runtime config to ./out
    dir: "{{.HOST}}"
    cmds:
      - dotnet run -- generate ./out

  # ── Local k3d deploy ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  deploy:local:
    desc: Build all component images in this system and import them into k3d-intropy
    vars:
      CLUSTER: intropy
      CONTEXT: k3d-intropy
      TAG: '{{.TAG | default "dev"}}'
      # Finds only files named exactly "Dockerfile" in this system's child
      # directories, so Dockerfile.debug / Dockerfile.validate variants are
      # excluded. Evaluated when a `for` loop templates the var, once per loop.
      DOCKERFILES:

**Nothing is broken, and nothing was written** — the conflict path is atomic, so the host record still declares only the two original components and the files are untouched.

1. **`--force` (recommended).** I ran it against a copy of your workspace; the overwrite is safe here. content.text:
Bug confirmed and fixed. Here's what was happening:

**Root cause**

You scaffolded with directory `tge` but name `Ssdf` — so the scaffold record carries `appId: "ssdf"` while living in the `tge/` folder. After `sys update` folded it in, the host correctly declares the component as `ssdf` (topology names come from the appId, not the directory).

But the flow diagram matched declared components to scaffolded integrations **by directory name alone**: it computed the expected path as `<system>/<component-name>` = `.../ssdf`, found nothing there, and concluded the scaffold at `.../tge` was undeclared — hence the phantom ghost. So you saw the declared "Ssdf" node *and* a ghost "tge" that were actually the same component.

**Fix** (in `buildDeclaredGraph`, `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`): matching now uses the scaffold record's `values.appId` — which is the same value the topology declares — falling back to the old path-shape match for records that predate appId. The ghost filter uses the same resolved path, so a matched scaffold can never appear as a ghost.

I simulated the exact join against your real workspace data (five declared components, scaffolds in `erp-extractor`, `wms-loader`, `oms-loader`, `web-loader`, and `tge`): before the fix `tge` was a ghost; after, all five match and the ghost list is empty. Typecheck and production build pass.

One thing worth knowing: the scaffold record also has `topic: "order-notification"` (singular) while the rest of the system uses `order-notifications` — so when you next update the host, Ssdf will subscribe to a *different* topic than everyone else. If that was a typo during scaffolding, fix the value in `tge/.intropy/scaffold.json` before running `sys update` again.

The FlowView changes are uncommitted on your branch alongside the earlier force-retry UI — say the word if you'd like both committed.
